title: Multi-employer bargaining streams
summary: From 6 June 2023 the supported and single-interest bargaining streams allow agreements to cover several employers.

instruments.title: Fair Work Legislation Amendment (Secure Jobs, Better Pay) Act 2022

commenced.what: Supported and single-interest bargaining streams commenced

direction_rationale: Coordinated wage setting across employers may raise wages in low-paid care sectors but reduces firm-level flexibility and can raise entry costs.
comparison: Employers with fewer than 20 employees are exempt from compulsion; building and construction excluded

verified.notes: Date from the Fair Work Commission's guide to the Act.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: New bargaining streams let one agreement cover several employers. It may lift pay in low-paid care sectors but sets common terms across competing employers and reduces firms' flexibility to organise work.

marks.reason: Common terms across employers reduce firms' flexibility to match pay and job design to their own productivity.
Competing employers bargaining together on labour costs dampens rivalry between them.
